newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopian cabinet approves lower expenditure.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopian cabinet approves lower expenditure.

text.p: Ethiopia's Council of Ministers (cabinet) on Tuesday approved sharply lower spending plans for 1997/98 with bolstering the economy and reducing poverty its main concerns, the state news agency ENA reported.
The ministers agreed on a government expenditure figure of 6.793 billion birr ($998.7 million) but did not give revenue forecasts or any indication of how the money would be raised.
The Council's approved proposals will now be presented to parliament for debate and final approval. No date for the presentation to parliament was immediately available.

Ethiopia's expenditure in the 1996/97 financial year (July-June) was posted at 9.75 billion birr. The finance ministry has not said what was expected in revenues in that period. It also did not say what the budget deficit in the 1996/97 financial year would be.
Economists said the smaller budget for 1997/98 was mainly on account of the Ethiopian birr, which has weakened to 6.8020 to the dollar from 6.38 in 1996/97.
"It is the currency, not anything to do with fiscal measures," said a senior independent economist in Addis Ababa.
ENA said that $551.6 million of forecast expenditure would go to the government's recurrent budget for programmes presented by various administrative organs in the country.

The balance of $447.1 million will go to development projects to be launched in 1997/98. These include repair or construction of roads, energy, transport and communications, agriculture development and education, ENA said.
Specific details of the budget will be available only when it goes to parliament and is formally presented by Prime Minister Meles Zenawi, government officials said.
The government of Meles, which overthrew Marxist dictator Mengistu Haile Mariam in 1991, has implemented Western-backed free market reforms designed to end poverty and build growth.
GDP growth for 1997/78 was projected at between nine and 10 percent compared with a drop in GDP of 7.4 percent in 1991/92. GDP growth reached 7.7 percent in 1995, official figures show.

Meles said has said in a report to parliament that economic performance during the first nine months of the 1996/97 fiscal year was "vigorous because of the strict fiscal policy that has been exercised in the country".
Government revenue exceeded expenditure to a greater extent than expected and the surplus was being used to service external debt, Meles's report added.
"Over the last nine months government revenue has exceeded expenditure by 844 million birr," Meles said.
